issue.title: fix(count_tokens): count custom-named deployments with their base_model's tokenizer
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description Token counts on a deployment whose name hides the model, like an Azure AI Foundry deployment called my-flash that serves DeepSeek-V4-Flash, now use the tokenizer of the base model the admin already set for cost tracking. Before this they fell back to OpenAI's tokenizer, so a short multilingual message counted 74 tokens where Azure bills 46. Deployments without a base model count the same as before, and when a base model's tokenizer is slow to download, the count waits at most 5 seconds and then counts the way it did before this PR
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Custom-named deployments ignore `base_model` when picking a tokenizer - A DeepSeek V4 deployment named `my-flash` counts with OpenAI's cl100k How it solves it: - The local estimate's tokenizer reads `model_info.base_model`, then `litellm_params.base_model` - The provider prefix is stripped like the deployment's own model name - OpenAI base models and the tool template from #49074 keep their path - A `base_model` tokenizer download slower than 5 seconds counts the way it did before
Decisions 1. Which value names the served model: `model_info.base_model`, then `litellm_params.base_model`, the order cost tracking, the token-count settings and #49074's tool template already use. A new per-deployment counting setting was the alternative, but admins already declare `base_model` for cost, so a second knob would only drift from it 2. Prefix: everything before the first `/` is dropped for the tokenizer, the same way the deployment's own `litellm_params.model` is trimmed before counting, so `azure_ai/deepseek-v4-flash` counts exactly like a deployment named `azure_ai/deepseek-v4-flash`. Keeping the prefix was the alternative, but the Anthropic and Cohere tokenizer checks compare bare names, so `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` would miss the Anthropic tokenizer. The tool template keeps the full name #49074 passes it, since its patterns match anywhere in the name 3. Scope: only the local estimate's tokenizer changes. The provider counting API still gets the real deployment name, since the provider routes on it, and `model_used` in the response still names the deployment 4. Slow tokenizer downloads: Llama and Cohere tokenizers come from the Hugging Face Hub, so a custom-named Llama deployment now starts a download it never started before. The count waits for it at most `TOKENIZER_LOAD_WAIT_SECONDS` (5 seconds, the limit the provider-failure path already uses), then counts the way the deployment counted before this PR, provider-failure fallback included, while the download keeps going in the background for later counts. These downloads get their own 4 load slots, so stuck ones never take the slots a provider-failure fallback needs. Without a limit, an earlier tip held every count on that deployment for over a minute with the Hub unreachable. `base_model` only changes the tokenizer when it names a different tokenizer than the deployment's own model, so `llama-3.3-70b` still waits for its own download whether or not it declares `base_model`. The bundled DeepSeek and Anthropic tokenizers and Hub tokenizers that already loaded skip the wait. Skipping Hub tokenizers for `base_model` was the other option, but it would leave Llama and Cohere deployments on the wrong tokenizer for good. A deployment with a `custom_tokenizer` keeps counting exactly as before, since that tokenizer wins over any model name 5. Open decision, spend and rate-limit estimates: when litellm estimates usage itself (failed-request spend rows, streams that return no usage, the Responses API output-limit estimate) and when the router reserves input tokens for a rate limit, it still reads `base_model` only for OpenAI models. Changing that changes billed spend and rate-limit decisions, needs the same download limit on those paths, and goes to LTS and main together, so it is filed as its own follow-up rather than folded into this PR 6. Base PR: #49074 (merged 2026-11-02) already renders tools with the base model's chat template, so this PR now carries only the tokenizer half. An open-PR search for base_model and token counting found nothing else covering it
## User Flow Before: a developer counts tokens on a custom-named DeepSeek deployment and gets a number far above what Azure bills 1. The proxy admin adds `my-flash` (`azure_ai/litellm-qa-count-alias` with `model_info.base_model: azure_ai/deepseek-v4-flash`) 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages/count_tokens with a short Japanese, Hindi and Russian message and `"model": "my-flash"` 3. The response says `{"input_tokens":74}` 4. The same body on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages bills 46 input tokens After: the same count is close to what Azure bills 1. The proxy admin adds `my-flash` (`azure_ai/litellm-qa-count-alias` with `model_info.base_model: azure_ai/deepseek-v4-flash`) 2. The developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages/count_tokens with a short Japanese, Hindi and Russian message and `"model": "my-flash"` 3. The response says `{"input_tokens":49}`, the same as a deployment named after the model 4. The same body on POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages bills 46 input tokens ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs run one config with three pairs of deployments, a deployment named after the model and a custom-named one that declares it as `base_model`. DeepSeek-V4-Flash runs on two Azure AI Foundry deployments. Llama 3.3 70B runs on Databricks, with `my-llama` going through a second LiteLLM proxy as a `hosted_vllm` server. Claude Sonnet 5.5 runs on Anthropic and on Databricks for `my-sonnet` The download legs send Hub requests to an address that never answers. The slots leg runs four custom-named Llama downloads at once on one worker. In the fallback leg Anthropic's count API answers 404, so `framed-probe` and `framed-llama` (with a Llama `base_model`) count locally For Llama and Claude the custom-named deployment now counts like the named one. Neither matches the bill, the same gap the named deployments already had | Case | Named after the model | Before | After | Billed | |---|---|---|---|---| | Multilingual, `my-flash` | 49 | 74 | 49 | 46 | | Multilingual, `my-llama` | 47 | 74 | 47 | 75 | | Multilingual, `my-sonnet` | 78 | 74 | 78 | 60 | | Text only, `my-flash` | 31 | 33 | 31 | 28 | | Text only, `my-llama` | 33 | 33 | 33 | 61 | | Text only, `my-sonnet` | 33 | 33 | 33 | 44 | | One tool, `my-flash` | 314 | 313 | 314 | 316 | | One tool, `my-llama` | 71 | 71 | 71 | Databricks 400 | | One tool, `my-sonnet` | 79 | 71 | 79 | 416 | | Download hangs, `my-llama` | n/a | 0.31 s | 5.83 s once | n/a | | Llama downloads hang, `my-flash` | 49 | 74 | 49 | 46 | | Llama downloads hang, `my-sonnet` | 78 | 74 | 78 | 60 | | Download hangs, `llama-3.3-70b` | n/a | over 20 s | over 20 s | n/a | | Count 404, `framed-llama` | n/a | 0.80 s | 6.29 s once | n/a | | Llama downloads hang, `framed-probe` | n/a | 23 | 23 | n/a | | Download hangs, `llama-3.3-70b-bm` | n/a | over 20 s | over 20 s | n/a | Counts are `/v1/messages/count_tokens` input tokens, except Claude's named column, which is `/utils/token_counter` since `/v1/messages/count_tokens` asks Anthropic there. Billed is `/v1/messages` usage
Config, second proxy and boot commands ```yaml model_list: - model_name: deepseek-v4-flash litellm_params: model: azure_ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_KEY - model_name: my-flash litellm_params: model: azure_ai/litellm-qa-count-alias api_base: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_AI_API_KEY model_info: base_model: azure_ai/deepseek-v4-flash - model_name: llama-3.3-70b litellm_params: model: databricks/databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct api_base: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_KEY - model_name: my-llama litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/my-llama api_base: os.environ/INNER_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct - model_name: claude-sonnet-5-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY - model_name: my-sonnet litellm_params: model: databricks/databricks-claude-sonnet-5-5 api_base: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_KEY model_info: base_model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` The second proxy that serves `my-llama`, booted with `--port $INNER_PORT --num_workers 1`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: my-llama litellm_params: model: databricks/databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct api_base: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/DATABRICKS_API_KEY ``` Env var names: `AZURE_AI_API_BASE`, `AZURE_AI_API_KEY`, `DATABRICKS_API_BASE`, `DATABRICKS_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, and `INNER_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:$INNER_PORT/v1`. Each proxy gets a fresh empty `HF_HOME` and `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` ```bash python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config config.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2 --timeout_worker_healthcheck 60 ``` For the download case, a second pair of proxies boots the same way with `HF_ENDPOINT=http://10.255.255.1`, an address that never answers, so the Llama 3 tokenizer download hangs The slots leg boots one more proxy per tree with `--num_workers 1` and the same `HF_ENDPOINT`, on this config plus three more custom-named Llama deployments ```yaml - model_name: my-llama-8b litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/my-llama-8b api_base: os.environ/INNER_API_BASE model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct - model_name: my-llama-1b litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/my-llama-1b api_base: os.environ/INNER_API_BASE model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct - model_name: my-llama-405b litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/my-llama-405b api_base: os.environ/INNER_API_BASE model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct ``` The fallback leg boots one more proxy per tree with `--num_workers 1` and the same `HF_ENDPOINT`, on this config, and runs `fallback.sh $PORT` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: framed-probe litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-count-probe-unknown api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY model_info: token_count_framing: 7 - model_name: framed-llama litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-count-probe-unknown api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct token_count_framing: 7 - model_name: llama-3.3-70b-bm litellm_params: model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 model_info: base_model: hosted_vllm/meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct # plus my-llama, my-llama-8b, my-llama-1b and my-llama-405b as above, with api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY ``` ```zsh #!/bin/zsh # usage: fallback.sh port=$1 key=$(cat ${0:A:h}/master_key) body() { print -r -- "{\"model\":\"$1\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the weather in Paris right now?\"}]}"; } call() { curl -s --max-time ${3:-60} -w ' [%{http_code} %{time_total}s]' localhost:$port/$1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$(body $2)"; } print "$(date -u +%T) POST /v1/messages/count_tokens framed-llama, first count on this worker -> $(call v1/messages/count_tokens framed-llama)" print "$(date -u +%T) POST /utils/token_counter llama-3.3-70b-bm, 20 s client timeout -> $(call utils/token_counter llama-3.3-70b-bm 20)" print "$(date -u +%T) POST /v1/messages/count_tokens framed-probe, before any Llama count -> $(call v1/messages/count_tokens framed-probe)" o=$(mktemp -d) for m in my-llama my-llama-8b my-llama-1b my-llama-405b; do call utils/token_counter $m > $o/$m & done wait for m in my-llama my-llama-8b my-llama-1b my-llama-405b; do print "$(date -u +%T) POST /utils/token_counter $m -> $(cat $o/$m)"; done print "$(date -u +%T) waiting 65 s so framed-probe's earlier tokenizer load is no longer reused" sleep 65 print "$(date -u +%T) POST /v1/messages/count_tokens framed-probe, while the four Llama downloads hang -> $(call v1/messages/count_tokens framed-probe)" print "$(date -u +%T) POST /v1/messages/count_tokens framed-llama again -> $(call v1/messages/count_tokens framed-llama)" ```
Scenario script, run as scenario3.sh counts|hang|named|slots $PORT ```zsh #!/bin/zsh # usage: scenario3.sh mode=$1; port=$2 Q=${0:A:h} key=$(cat $Q/master_key) tool_body() { print -r -- "{\"model\":\"$1\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is the weather in Paris right now?\"}],\"tools\":[{\"name\":\"get_weather\",\"description\":\"Get the current weather for a city\",\"input_schema\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"city\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"description\":\"City name\"},\"unit\":{\"type\":\"string\",\"enum\":[\"celsius\",\"fahrenheit\"]}},\"required\":[\"city\"]}}]}"; } text_body() { print -r -- "{\"model\":\"$1\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Summarize the plot of Hamlet in two sentences, naming the main characters and how the play ends for each of them.\"}]}"; } multi_body() { print -r -- "{\"model\":\"$1\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Translate to English: 東京の天気は今日晴れです。मुंबई में आज बारिश हो रही है। В Москве сегодня идёт снег.\"}]}"; } nomax() { print -r -- "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; b=json.load(sys.stdin); b.pop("max_tokens"); print(json.dumps(b, ensure_ascii=False))'; } usage_of() { print -r -- "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps(d.get("usage", d)))'; } post() { curl -s --max-time ${3:-120} localhost:$port/$1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2"; } timed() { curl -s --max-time 60 -o $3 -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s' localhost:$port/$1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$2"; } case $mode in counts) for shape in ${=SHAPES:-tool text multi}; do print "## $shape" for m in ${=MODELS:-deepseek-v4-flash my-flash llama-3.3-70b my-llama claude-sonnet-5-5 my-sonnet}; do b=$(${shape}_body $m) print -r -- "POST /v1/messages/count_tokens $m -> $(post v1/messages/count_tokens "$b")" print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter $m -> $(post utils/token_counter "$(nomax "$b")")" print -r -- "POST /v1/messages $m -> usage $(usage_of "$(post v1/messages "$b")")" done done ;; hang) b=$(nomax "$(text_body my-llama)") o=$(mktemp -d) print "first count sent at $(date -u +%T)" timed utils/token_counter "$b" $o/1 > $o/1.t & sleep 1 print "second count sent at $(date -u +%T), while the first is loading" timed v1/messages/count_tokens "$(text_body my-llama)" $o/2 > $o/2.t & wait print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter my-llama -> $(cat $o/1.t) $(cat $o/1)" print -r -- "POST /v1/messages/count_tokens my-llama -> $(cat $o/2.t) $(cat $o/2)" print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter my-llama, sent after both answered -> $(timed utils/token_counter "$b" $o/3) $(cat $o/3)" ;; slots) o=$(mktemp -d) llamas=(my-llama my-llama-8b my-llama-1b my-llama-405b) print "four custom-named Llama counts sent at $(date -u +%T)" for m in $llamas; do timed utils/token_counter "$(nomax "$(multi_body $m)")" $o/$m > $o/$m.t & done sleep 1 print "custom-named DeepSeek and Claude counts sent at $(date -u +%T), while the four Llama downloads hang" for m in my-flash my-sonnet; do print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter $m -> $(timed utils/token_counter "$(nomax "$(multi_body $m)")" $o/$m) $(cat $o/$m)" done wait for m in $llamas; do print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter $m -> $(cat $o/$m.t) $(cat $o/$m)" done ;; named) b=$(nomax "$(multi_body llama-3.3-70b)") print "count on llama-3.3-70b, which declares no base_model, sent at $(date -u +%T) with a 20 s client timeout" print -r -- "POST /utils/token_counter llama-3.3-70b -> $(curl -s --max-time 20 -o $Q/named_body.$port -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}s' localhost:$port/utils/token_counter -H "Authorization: Bearer $key" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$b") $(cat $Q/named_body.$port 2>/dev/null)" ;; esac ```
### Before (1df1c4074b) #### Multilingual 1. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-flash` -> `{"input_tokens":74}` where `deepseek-v4-flash` gives 49, and `/v1/messages` bills 46 on both 2. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-llama` -> `{"input_tokens":74}` where `llama-3.3-70b` gives 47, and `/v1/messages` bills 75 on both 3. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-sonnet` -> `{"input_tokens":74}` where `/utils/token_counter` on `claude-sonnet-5-5` gives 78, and `/v1/messages` bills 60 on both 4. `/utils/token_counter` on all three -> `"tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer"` #### Text only
Steps 1. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-flash` -> `{"input_tokens":33}` where `deepseek-v4-flash` gives 31, and `/v1/messages` bills 28 on both 2. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-llama` -> `{"input_tokens":33}`, the same as `llama-3.3-70b` for this text, and `/v1/messages` bills 61 on both 3. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-sonnet` -> `{"input_tokens":33}`, the same as `claude-sonnet-5-5`'s local count for this text, and `/v1/messages` bills 44 on both 4. `/utils/token_counter` on all three -> `"tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer"`
#### One tool
Steps 1. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-flash` -> `{"input_tokens":313}` where `deepseek-v4-flash` gives 314, and `/v1/messages` bills 316 on both (60 plus 256 cache reads) 2. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-llama` -> `{"input_tokens":71}`, the same as `llama-3.3-70b`, and `/v1/messages` answers 400 from Databricks on both ("Model response did not respect the required format") 3. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-sonnet` -> `{"input_tokens":71}` where `/utils/token_counter` on `claude-sonnet-5-5` gives 79, and `/v1/messages` bills 416 on both 4. `/utils/token_counter` on all three -> `"tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer"`
#### Tokenizer download hangs
Steps 1. `/utils/token_counter` on `my-llama` -> 200 in 0.31 s, `{"total_tokens":33,"tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer"}`, since nothing is downloaded 2. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `my-llama`, sent 1 s later -> 200 in 0.30 s, `{"input_tokens":33}` 3. The next `/utils/token_counter` -> 200 in 0.01 s
#### Llama downloads hang
Steps 1. `/utils/token_counter` on `llama-3.3-70b`, which declares no `base_model`, gets no answer within the 20 s client timeout, since it waits for its tokenizer download 2. Four `/utils/token_counter` calls on `my-llama`, `my-llama-8b`, `my-llama-1b` and `my-llama-405b` -> 200 in 0.48 to 0.70 s, `{"total_tokens":74,"tokenizer_type":"openai_tokenizer"}`, since nothing is downloaded 3. `/utils/token_counter` on `my-flash` and `my-sonnet`, sent 1 s later -> 74 with `openai_tokenizer` on both
#### Provider count fails
Steps 1. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `framed-llama` -> 200 in 0.80 s, `{"input_tokens":23,"litellm_count_source":"local_estimate"}`, since Anthropic's 404 falls back to the local estimate 2. `/utils/token_counter` on `llama-3.3-70b-bm`, named after its model and declaring it as `base_model`, gets no answer within the 20 s client timeout, since it waits for its tokenizer download 3. Four `/utils/token_counter` calls on `my-llama`, `my-llama-8b`, `my-llama-1b` and `my-llama-405b` -> 200 in 0.18 to 0.22 s with `openai_tokenizer` 4. `/v1/messages/count_tokens` on `framed-probe`, sent 65 s later -> 200 in 0.18 s, `{"input_tokens":23,"litellm_count_source":"local_estimate"}`

issue.title: fix(guardrails)!: mask the prompt in failure logs for logging_only Presidio
issue.body:
Presidio's `logging_only` mode now masks the prompt in failed chat calls' logs too. Before, a failed call sent raw names and emails to Langfuse and every other logger

[/stupid: What the PR adds](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/6604f11813979f015f152efad525289a/raw/BerriAI-litellm-49057-stupid-purpose.html)

[/stupid: What breaks](https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://gist.githubusercontent.com/mateo-berri/623d070e57651bfa869dafa2ea9ce663/raw/BerriAI-litellm-49057-stupid.html)

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

Breaking change: with a Presidio or Guardrails AI `logging_only` guardrail, failed chat calls return errors up to 1 s later. Check client timeouts before upgrading

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Presidio `logging_only` masked success logs only
- Failed calls logged the raw prompt to every logger

How it solves it:

- Mask a copy before the failure log is built, spend log included
- A mask that errors or takes over 1 s logs it redacted

## User Flow

Before: a team using Presidio `logging_only` ships real names and emails to Langfuse whenever a call fails

1. The admin adds a Presidio `logging_only` guardrail and the Langfuse callback, then starts the proxy
2. A client sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with a name and email in the prompt and a parameter OpenAI rejects
3. The client gets OpenAI's 400 back
4. The failed request's Langfuse trace shows the real name and email

After: the failed request's trace is masked like a successful one

1. Same setup
2. Same request
3. Same 400
4. The Langfuse trace shows `<PERSON>` and `<EMAIL_ADDRESS>` instead

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg ran a 2-worker proxy with real Presidio or Guardrails AI, `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, and Langfuse. Cases 1 to 4, 9, 10, 20, 21 and 23 to 27 ran at 0a7c61aab0 against the merge base 07c7229895, with Postgres. The other cases ran at 997d27d27c against 24afa12253

Last updated: 0a7c61aab0. QA ran on 0a7c61aab0 for cases 1 to 4, 9, 10, 20, 21 and 23 to 27, on afc2516dd1 for case 23's 8 run check, and on 997d27d27c for the rest. Changes since 997d27d27c: nine fixes, two test-only commits and three main merges, listed under Setup. The other cases still hold because main's changes there are on the success and response paths, their routing paths re-ran here, none rewrites the prompt, which 7091cf5c7e acts on, and each has the guardrail 0a7c61aab0 checks for. Verification: G4 matched at 83e74b9ec8, and cases 1 to 4, 9, 10, 20, 21 and 23 to 25 matched their afc2516dd1 results at 0a7c61aab0

<details>
<summary>Setup</summary>

Changes since 997d27d27c: 4042a605af merges the masked prompt into the live log, d9b1bafc17 merges main, a247d9e553 moves the time-bound tests to controlled clocks, b0f9a0fa6d defers sync loggers on a cancel, adf967ed73 drops exception text from the mask error log, d16efa05d6 merges main, 0232e11705 moves the masking tests to in-memory Presidio and Guardrails AI, 83e74b9ec8 masks the Supabase failure row, 7ab295df0a merges main, which moves chat routing to the Rust router core, cc92dffa8c masks a refused pick's failure log before its fallback starts, cfd0d4cadc logs a refused pick before its fallback starts, afc2516dd1 makes a later failure log wait for the mask, 7091cf5c7e logs a prompt copy redacted when it differs from the prompt the mask ran on, and 0a7c61aab0 skips the mask when no logging-only guardrail runs for the request. Main's changes to the logging, Presidio and Guardrails AI files are on the success and response paths. 7091cf5c7e changes only a logged copy that holds a different prompt than the mask saw, and neither it nor 0a7c61aab0 touches which deployment a failure log names

The 0a7c61aab0 run's config, with Postgres, the refused `gpt-primary` deployment, case 21's fallback and case 26's prompt template, is at the end of its [gist file](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/740bd95f46f002aaf7b5e827f59430b0#file-gist-rerun-0a7c61aab0-md). Case 25 booted it without the template and with `cancel_on_disconnect: true`, and case 27 without the `guardrails` section. The config below is the 997d27d27c run's

`config.yaml`

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-mini
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: gpt-mini-broken
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: sk-qa-deliberately-invalid-key
  - model_name: gpt-mini-badkey
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: sk-qa-deliberately-invalid-key
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: presidio-log
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: presidio
      mode: logging_only
      presidio_analyzer_api_base: http://127.0.0.1:30098/
      presidio_anonymizer_api_base: http://127.0.0.1:24666/
  - guardrail_name: block-word
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: litellm_content_filter
      mode: pre_call
      blocked_words:
        - keyword: "qa-forbidden-word"
          action: BLOCK
router_settings:
  fallbacks: [{"gpt-mini-broken": ["gpt-mini"]}]
litellm_settings:
  callbacks: custom_callbacks.proxy_handler_instance
  success_callback: ["langfuse"]
  failure_callback: ["langfuse"]
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

`custom_callbacks.py` is a small `CustomLogger` whose `async_log_success_event` and `async_log_failure_event` append the event name, `litellm_call_id`, `kwargs["messages"]`, and `kwargs["standard_logging_object"]["messages"]` to `capture.jsonl`

```sh
docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:30098:3000 mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-analyzer:latest
docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:24666:3000 mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-anonymizer:latest
litellm --config config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2
P='My name is Jane Doe and my email is jane.doe@example.com. Reply with my first name spelled backwards in lowercase and nothing else.'
```

The reply `enaj` is not PII, so it shows which prompt the model really got

Cases 11, 12 and 14 send the multi-turn bodies the script at the top of each [gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/0b164941ffa005aa6c166b77000a5bee) file builds

Cases 16 to 18 boot the same config with Postgres added (`database_url` and `store_prompts_in_spend_logs: true` under `general_settings`) and a second guardrail `presidio-pre` in `mode: pre_call` that a request turns on with `"guardrails": ["presidio-pre"]`. Case 20 adds `gpt-mini-timeout` (`timeout: 0.05`) and sends `"num_retries": 1`. Case 21 adds `gpt-mini-bad-a` and `gpt-mini-bad-b`, both with invalid keys, and the fallback `{"gpt-mini-bad-a": ["gpt-mini-bad-b"]}`. Case 19 is a plain Python script that puts the Presidio guardrail in `logging_only` mode and a `CustomLogger` printing `kwargs["messages"]` in `litellm.callbacks`, then calls sync `litellm.completion(..., reasoning_effort="bogus")` 3 times. Case 22 runs it with the Guardrails AI guardrail below

G1 to G3 swap Presidio for a real Guardrails AI server (guardrails-ai 0.9.3, guardrails-api 0.3.3) whose guard replaces the name and email with `<PERSON>` and `<EMAIL_ADDRESS>`, and raises on text holding `qa-reject-word`

```yaml
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: guardrails-ai-log
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: guardrails_ai
      mode: logging_only
      guard_name: qa-mask-pii
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:30723
      guardrails_ai_api_input_format: llmOutput
```

</details>

| Case | Before | After
|---|---|---
| 1, 2. Chat call fails (400), streamed or not | Raw | Masked
| 3. Bad key falls back, both reply `enaj` | Raw | Masked
| 9, 10, 15. Bad virtual key, or Presidio hung or stopped | Raw | Redacted
| 11, 12. 19 or 59 turns fail, x3 | Raw | Masked, redacted
| 13, 14. 20 parallel case 1, 19 turns blocked x3 | Raw | Masked
| 16, 17. Rate limited (429), or case 1 with Postgres | Raw | Masked
| 19, 22, G1, G3. SDK fails x3, Guardrails AI fails or raises | Raw | Masked, redacted
| 20, 21, 23. Retry or fallback fails, or rejected then falls back | Raw | Masked
| 24. Rejected, then its fallback fails | Raw | Masked
| 25. Client hangs up mid-mask | Raw, 6 of 6 | Masked, 6 of 6
| 26. Prompt template call fails | Raw | Masked, body redacted
| 27. Case 26, no guardrail | Raw | Raw
| 23. Failure log names the rejected deployment, x8 | 8 of 8 | 8 of 8
| G4. Flagged prompt, proxy error log | Prompt (b0f9a0fa6d) | None

Cells are what Langfuse and the logger got, plus spend logs for 16, 17 and the afc2516dd1 run

### 1. Chat call fails

1. Send a call OpenAI rejects. Both legs answer 400, Before as `7e631826`

<details>
<summary>Command</summary>

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Severe

- Every failed, rejected, or blocked chat call (429s, over-budget keys, guardrail blocks) waits up to 1 s on Presidio or Guardrails AI before its error returns, with no setting to skip it. Retries and fallbacks start later, and Presidio needs room for failure traffic. Live QA added 0.3 to 1 s.

### Medium

- A long chat or a loaded Presidio past the 1 s limit logs redacted. A 59-turn chat did 3 of 3 times, and 4 of 20 parallel failures in one run

### Low

- Presidio scans run in parallel again, as before #19714
- /v1/messages, /v1/responses, and sync `completion()` in a running event loop log failures raw, as before
- OTel and Arize spans read the raw request body, as before
- Each sync Presidio mask leaves an HTTP session open, like sync successes
- Mid-stream failures lack live proof, since no provider fails on demand
- The sync SDK logs Guardrails AI failures redacted, as it has no sync hook

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

<details>
<summary>Decisions</summary>

1. Which hooks run on failure
   - Chosen: only guardrails that mask the logged request, marked by a new `masks_logged_request` class flag that Presidio and Guardrails AI set, since both rewrite the logged prompt
   - Not chosen: every `logging_only` guardrail. Audit guardrails (Purview, XecGuard) would call their vendors inline before the error reaches the client and before router retries, and failure scans for the generic guardrails are #48314's, run in the background
   - Not chosen: every `CustomLogger` logging hook as on success, which would also run success-only work such as the rate limit header mirror on failures
2. Where the mask runs
   - Chosen: before the failure log payload is built, so `standard_logging_object["messages"]` comes from the masked copy with no second mirroring step
   - Not chosen: mask afterwards and mirror into the payload, the way #35954 does for successes
3. What the mask touches
   - Chosen: a deep copy of `messages`, since Presidio masks message dicts in place and the router resends the caller's dicts on retries and fallbacks
   - Not chosen: mask in place like the success path, which would send `<PERSON>` to the fallback model
   - Chosen: every other logged field that holds the same prompt (`input`, the `messages` the proxy puts in `optional_params`, the proxy request body in the log payload, and the request body the proxy hands its failure hooks) gets the masked list too, which the success path gets for free by masking in place. Langfuse's model parameters and the spend log's request body read those fields
   - Chosen: a field counts as a copy when its messages equal the raw prompt, since the proxy's request body keeps its own list
   - Chosen: a copy that holds a different prompt than the mask saw, because a template or an earlier hook rewrote it, logs redacted
   - Not chosen: keep that copy as it is, which stored the client's raw prompt in the spend row's request body (case 26)
   - Chosen: the mask, and so this redaction, runs only when a logging-only guardrail masks the request, so a proxy without one logs as before (case 27)
   - Not chosen: claim the mask on every failure, which redacted a template call's request body on proxies that never mask (7091cf5c7e)
   - Chosen: the Supabase failure row gets the masked prompt once a mask ran, else the request's own messages, so a prompt management rewrite still shows there
   - Not chosen: match only the same list object, which leaves a copied body raw
   - Not chosen: run Presidio once per copy, which multiplies the inline wait
   - Chosen: only the masked prompt and its copies go back into the live log state, and only where they still hold the raw prompt, so a fallback that started during the mask keeps its own deployment
   - Not chosen: write the whole masked copy back, which logged a fallback's reply under the rejected deployment (live at 997d27d27c)
   - Chosen: when a router retry or fallback also fails, the proxy's failure hooks get the request body the failure log carried, since each attempt resets the logged messages to the raw prompt. The spend log stays masked
4. When it runs
   - Chosen: inline on the async failure path, before the error is raised to the caller, so every failure logger (sync and async) sees the masked copy. A failed call waits for one Presidio pass, 0.6 to 1.3 s in live QA, and a call a guardrail blocks went from 0.04 s to 0.4 s
   - Chosen: a 1 s bound. A 59-turn failed chat on a loaded box ran past it and logged redacted
   - Not chosen: 3 s or more, which masks longer chats but triples the worst-case wait on every failed call while Presidio is slow
   - Not chosen: no bound, which let a hung Presidio hold every failed request's error response
   - Not chosen: in the background, which would change failure logger ordering and the router's one-failure-log dedupe, and the router's cooldown callbacks share the failure callback list with the loggers
   - Chosen: when a masking guardrail runs, a pick the router turns away before the call (a pre-call check) runs both failure handlers before its fallback starts, the order the client wrapper uses, since the fallback reuses the request's logging object and resets its prompt and deployment. Without one, the refused pick is still logged in the background
   - Not chosen: await only the mask and log in the background, which logged the raw prompt under the fallback in 5 of 8 live runs (cc92dffa8c)
   - Not decided yet: a setting to skip or shorten the wait. The owner picks in the signoff
   - The router's wait for a broken stream's failure log grows by the 1 s mask limit only when a masking guardrail runs, so other deployments keep the old 1 s
5. Sync failure handler on an event loop
   - Chosen: it skips masking when a loop is running in its thread, and every async path masks first, so the loop is never blocked on Presidio's worker thread
   - Callers that run the sync handler first on the loop (file streaming, MCP tools) stay unmasked, and Presidio only masks chat calls, so nothing changes there today
6. A mask that raises or runs out of time
   - Chosen: either one, or a sync mask the full logging queue drops, logs the request redacted, the same fields `turn_off_message_logging` drops, on the async path and the sync SDK path alike
   - Not chosen: log the raw prompt, as a success-path mask error does today, which would leak exactly when Presidio is down or overloaded
   - Chosen: on the sync path, a guardrail with only an async logging hook (Guardrails AI) logs redacted, since the sync path calls only the sync hook, as the sync success path does
   - Not chosen: run its async hook on a new event loop in the mask thread, which no sync logging path does today
   - Chosen: the sync mask runs on its own thread pool, and a mask still queued at its time limit is cancelled, so a hung Presidio cannot hold the shared logging workers
   - Chosen: the mask error log names only the exception type and the guardrail, since a guardrail's error can carry the prompt
   - Chosen: a sync hook that returns something other than a `(kwargs, result)` pair logs redacted, like a hook that raises
   - Not chosen: log the traceback, which printed a flagged prompt from Guardrails AI's response (G4 at b0f9a0fa6d)
7. Requests rejected before reaching the model
   - Chosen: an authenticated rejection is masked by Presidio like any failure
   - Chosen: an unauthenticated one (a bad virtual key) is redacted with no Presidio call, so anyone without a key cannot make the proxy run Presidio
8. The async failure is marked logged before the mask is awaited, so two concurrent failure notifications still log once
9. A caller cancelled during the mask
   - Chosen: the mask runs as a shielded task, and both failure handlers (router cooldowns, sync and async loggers) run once it ends, redacted first when loop shutdown cancels the mask
   - Not chosen: let the cancel drop the handlers, which would skip the failed deployment's cooldown and its failure logs
10. Provider-billed failure usage is estimated on the prompt sent to the model, never the masked log copy, since placeholders change the token count
11. Presidio's shared HTTP session
   - Chosen: hold its lock only while creating the session, so the scans of one request and of concurrent requests run in parallel
   - Not chosen: hold it for the whole request as before, which made every Presidio call in a worker, pre-call masking too, wait for the one ahead of it
   - #19190 held the lock only while creating the session, and #19714 moved the session's use inside the lock, which made every scan wait. This restores #19190's parallel scans
12. Base PR: none. #48314 audits failed calls for generic guardrails only and skips own-hook guardrails like Presidio, and #35954 only mirrors masked messages into the success-path payload

</details>

<details>
<summary>/live-pr-risk</summary>

Ran at 0a7c61aab0 against the merge base 07c7229895, each side a 2-worker proxy with Postgres, real Presidio, real `gpt-5.4-mini` and Langfuse. The walk for cfd0d4cadc and afc2516dd1 followed the router's refused-pick path and every caller of the failure-log mask (the SDK wrapper, the failure dispatch, the async failure handler, the router, and the proxy's own failure hook), and it added case 24, a refused pick whose fallback also fails, and case 25, a client hang-up during the mask with `cancel_on_disconnect` on. The walk for 7091cf5c7e followed both readers of the prompt copies it rewrites, the failure log payload every failure logger reads and the request body the proxy hands its failure hooks and spend row, and it added case 26, a failed call through a prompt template. The walk for 0a7c61aab0 followed every caller of the two mask entry points (the SDK wrapper, both failure handlers, and the Rust router, which already checked for a masking guardrail), and it added case 27, case 26 on proxies with no guardrail. Cases 1 to 4, 9, 10, 20, 21, 23 and 24 ran on the default config, case 25 on a fresh boot, and cases 26 and 27 with the template, and all of them matched the merge base on status and differed only in masked or redacted failure logs. Case 23's 8 run deployment check ran at afc2516dd1

Earlier, 4042a605af ran against 24afa12253 with a logging proxy in front of OpenAI, Anthropic and Langfuse, so the outbound requests were compared too. 17 scenarios on chat, streaming, fallbacks, retries, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, embeddings, auth errors and key lifecycle matched on status and outbound requests, and differed only in what the PR names (masked failure logs). The merged tree d9b1bafc17 re-ran cases 1, 3, 20 and 23 with the same results. b0f9a0fa6d changes only when a cancelled failure dispatch hands the sync loggers their log, so its focused walk re-ran those 4 cases, whose Langfuse failure logs go through that changed handoff, and they matched again. adf967ed73 changes only the text of the mask error log, whose one reader is the operator, so its focused walk ran G4 against b0f9a0fa6d, and the log lost the prompt while the failure logger still got the redacted request. d16efa05d6 merges main, which changes the logging, proxy, Presidio, and guardrail files this PR touches, so cases 1, 3, 20, 23 and G4 re-ran there and matched again. 83e74b9ec8 changes what the Supabase failure row gets and makes a sync mask hook that returns no pair log redacted instead of stopping the sync failure loggers, so its focused walk re-ran those 5 cases, whose sync Langfuse failure logs go through that hook result, and they matched

Breaking

- At 997d27d27c a fallback after a pre-call rejection logged its reply under the rejected deployment, spend rows included. Fixed in 4042a605af, and case 23 names the fallback deployment 4 of 4 times at d9b1bafc17 and b0f9a0fa6d
- The failure log of a call rejected before a fallback, which the router's failure callback also reads, could name the fallback deployment. It showed at the old merge base 24afa12253 (2 of 4 runs fully, 1 partly), and hit 4 of 4 at d9b1bafc17 and 8 of 8 at 7ab295df0a. Fixed in cfd0d4cadc, and case 23 names the refused deployment 8 of 8 times at afc2516dd1, as the current merge base does
- At cfd0d4cadc, a client hang-up during a refused pick's mask, with `cancel_on_disconnect` on, logged the raw prompt in 2 of 6 calls to Langfuse, the capture logger and the spend row. The proxy's 499 path puts the raw prompt back, and its failure log did not wait for the running mask. Fixed in afc2516dd1, and case 25 logged masked 12 of 12 times over two fresh boots, where the merge base logged raw 6 of 6
- At 7091cf5c7e, a failed template call on a proxy with no masking guardrail logged its request body redacted, in a unit test Greptile's finding prompted. Fixed in 0a7c61aab0, and case 27 matches the merge base 3 of 3 times

Backward incompatible

- Failed chat calls with a masking guardrail return their error up to 1 s later (the Severe caveat). Approval: pending, asked in the severe signoff
- A mask that errors or runs past 1 s logs the request redacted, where it was raw before (Decision 6)
- With a logging-only masking guardrail, a logged request body holding a different prompt than the mask saw logs redacted, where it was raw before (Decision 3)
- Presidio scans of one worker run in parallel again (Decision 11)

Regression risk, not reached live

- A refused pick under `max_parallel_requests` holds its deployment slot through the mask, up to 1 s, as a provider failure already does
- A cancel between marking the failure logged and the mask drops the async failure log
- `compact_to_fit` calls estimate billed failure usage on the first attempt's messages
- A final mid-stream failure leaves the spend request body raw
- A sync mask that raises in its thread pool drops the sync failure log, and a hung one holds a pool thread
- A custom guardrail that masks only inside its own `async_logging_hook` keeps raw failure logs, since it lacks the new class flag
- Test doubles that stand in a `MagicMock` logging object fail on the async error path

Dependency graph

| Dependent | Status
|---|---
| Presidio async mask | verified-live
| Presidio sync SDK mask | verified-live
| Guardrails AI async and sync | verified-live
| Router retries and fallbacks | verified-live
| Router refused-pick log | verified-live
| Proxy failure hooks and spend rows | verified-live
| Prompt template failures | verified-live
| Proxies with no masking guardrail | verified-live
| Proxy 499 on hang-up | verified-live
| Auth error redaction | verified-live
| Langfuse and custom loggers | verified-live
| `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses` | verified-live, unchanged
| Router cooldown callback | untested
| Mid-stream fallback wait | unit-tested
| Purview, XecGuard, base hook | unit-tested
| Registry loggers | unit-tested
| Prometheus failure hook | untested
| Rust bridge failure handler | untested
| Supabase failure row | unit-tested

Not verified

- Router cooldowns, since the rig ran with them off
- `compact_to_fit` and mid-stream failures, since no provider fails on demand
- The Rust bridge failure handler
- The Supabase failure row, since QA has no Supabase project

Legacy suites

Ran the 135 legacy integration files that reach the changed modules, at 4042a605af before the main merge. No red came from this PR. Every red failed the same way when rerun on the merge base: accounting 2, database harness timeouts, extensions 8, mcp 3, and providers 12, plus 32 mcp errors from a test server that needs mcp below 2 on both sides. One more extensions red passed on both reruns, and cost, management, sdk, and security passed

</details>

</details>

<summary>Bugbot summary</summary>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes failure logging and PII handling across proxy, router, and SDK paths with a user-visible latency change and complex async cancellation behavior; regressions could leak prompts or block cooldown/logging.
> 
> **Overview**
> Failed chat and proxy paths now run **logging-only** guardrails that opt in via `masks_logged_request` (Presidio and Guardrails AI) **before** failure callbacks build payloads, so Langfuse, spend logs, Supabase, and proxy failure hooks see masked prompts instead of raw text. Masking updates the failure log copy only (`messages`, `input`, `proxy_server_request`, and related copies); the prompt sent to the model and token billing stay on the unmasked content.
> 
> The failure mask is bounded by **`FAILURE_LOG_MASK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (1s)** on async and sync paths. Timeouts, mask errors, hung Presidio, auth-only rejections, or async-only hooks on sync calls **redact** the request. Cancellation and router **refused-pick** flows await masking (or defer handlers) so fallbacks do not leak raw prompts or mis-attribute deployments; mid-stream failure waits can extend by the mask timeout.
> 
> **Breaking:** authenticated failures with these guardrails may return errors up to ~1s later while masking runs.

issue.title: feat(gemini): translate prompt_cache_breakpoint to Gemini context caching on chat completions
issue.body:
OpenAI's `prompt_cache_breakpoint` marker on a chat completions content part now turns on Gemini context caching for `gemini/` and `vertex_ai/` models, the same way `cache_control` already does. Before this, the marker was ignored, so the marked prefix went out in full on every call and only Gemini's partial implicit caching ever kicked in

The marker's ttl carries over to the Gemini cache (30m by default, or 12h). A malformed marker follows the usual `drop_params` rule, so it gets dropped with `drop_params` on and answers 400 without it

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Gemini models ignore OpenAI's `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on chat completions
- A marked prompt never creates a Gemini cache, so every call pays full price

How it solves it:

- A marked part is cached like the same part with `cache_control`
- The marker's ttl (30m by default, or 12h) becomes the cache ttl
- A malformed marker answers 400, or is dropped under `drop_params`

<details>
<summary>Design decisions</summary>

1. A marked part is rewritten as the same part with `cache_control` before the cached prefix is split off, so it reuses the existing cache key, ttl handling, minimum-size check, and rejected-cache retry. The alternative was a separate marker path in the caching code, which would duplicate all of that
2. A marker with no ttl uses OpenAI's 30m default (sent to Gemini as 1800s), not Gemini's own 1h default, since the caller asked for OpenAI's semantics
3. `30m` and `12h` pass through as 1800s and 43200s, since Gemini accepts any ttl
4. A malformed marker (a wrong or missing `mode`, a ttl other than 30m or 12h, an unknown key like `tll`, or a non-object) answers 400 without `drop_params` and is dropped with it, leaving the part uncached. The alternative was falling back to the default ttl, which would hide a typo like `tll` behind a silent 30m cache
5. A `cache_control` already on the part wins over the marker. A malformed marker there still answers 400, since the OpenAI param is invalid either way
6. Only markers on content parts are read. Message-level markers, tool markers, and `prompt_cache_options` are out of scope
7. The 400 also applies when `disable_anthropic_gemini_context_caching_transform` is on, for the same reason as 5
8. An explicit `null` marker counts as no marker

</details>

## User Flow

Before: a developer marks a long system prompt with `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on a Gemini model, and Gemini never caches it

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for a `gemini/` or `vertex_ai/` model with an ~8k-token system part carrying `"prompt_cache_breakpoint": {"mode": "explicit"}`
2. The response has no `cache_creation_input_tokens`
3. They send the same request again and get `cached_tokens` of 6105 out of 8100 at best on `gemini/`, and a flat 4077 on `vertex_ai/`
4. A marker like `{"mode": "implicit"}` is ignored too, and the request goes through uncached

After: the same request creates a Gemini cache and the second call reads the whole marked prefix from it

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for a `gemini/` or `vertex_ai/` model with an ~8k-token system part carrying `"prompt_cache_breakpoint": {"mode": "explicit"}`
2. The response reports `cache_creation_input_tokens` for the marked prefix
3. They send the same request again and get `cached_tokens` covering the whole marked prefix
4. A marker like `{"mode": "implicit"}` gets a 400 naming `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, or is dropped when they send `"drop_params": true`

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Each leg runs two proxies from its own worktree with `--num_workers 2` and no DB. Call 1 goes to proxy A and call 2 sends the same body to proxy B, so the cache has to work across processes. Every body carries a fresh ~8k-token document. The scripts and full raw output are in [this gist](https://gist.github.com/mateo-berri/a8be858f6256ce25d46f42a0ce2b8c7d)

```yaml
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-3.8-flash

  - model_name: vertex-gemini-flash

      vertex_location: global
```

issue.title: fix(realtime): keep push-to-talk for transcription sessions opened without intent under a transcript guardrail
issue.body:
With a `realtime_input_transcription` guardrail on, a push-to-talk transcription session on Vertex Chirp or Meta Muse gets switched to server VAD when the client connects without `?intent=transcription`, which is what the OpenAI SDK's `client.realtime.connect(model=...)` does by default. The client sends `turn_detection: null`, the proxy swaps it for `server_vad`, and one commit comes back as several transcripts split at every pause

For these providers the proxy builds the `session.created` event itself, and that event already says the session is a transcription session. It just never reached the check that decides whether to apply the guardrail's VAD gate. This PR runs the event through that check before it goes to the client, so transcription sessions keep the client's `turn_detection` and voice sessions still get the gate. The check still ignores the session type the client declares, as #44843 intended

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Push-to-talk transcription without `intent` gets forced to server VAD
- One committed recording comes back split into several transcripts
- Only with a `realtime_input_transcription` guardrail on, Chirp and Muse

How it solves it:

- The proxy-built `session.created` now marks transcription sessions
- Transcription sessions keep the client's `turn_detection: null`
- Voice sessions still get `server_vad` with `create_response: false`

## User Flow

Before: a developer's push-to-talk transcription app gets one recording back as two transcripts

1. The proxy admin turns on a `realtime_input_transcription` guardrail for `chirp-3` (Vertex Chirp 3)
2. The app opens `wss://litellm-domain/v1/realtime?model=chirp-3` with the OpenAI SDK, no `intent` query
3. It sends `session.update` with `type: transcription` and `audio.input.turn_detection: null`
4. `session.updated` comes back with `turn_detection` set to `server_vad`
5. It streams 7.7 s of speech and commits once, and gets two transcripts split at the pause

After: the same app gets one transcript for its one commit

1. The proxy admin turns on a `realtime_input_transcription` guardrail for `chirp-3` (Vertex Chirp 3)
2. The app opens `wss://litellm-domain/v1/realtime?model=chirp-3` with the OpenAI SDK, no `intent` query
3. It sends `session.update` with `type: transcription` and `audio.input.turn_detection: null`
4. `session.updated` comes back with `turn_detection: null`
5. It streams 7.7 s of speech and commits once, and gets one transcript with both sentences

Each leg boots one proxy with 2 workers from its own tree, `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2`, and drives it with the OpenAI Python SDK (`openai` 3.37.0) realtime client against live Vertex Chirp 3 and OpenAI. The audio is a 7.7 s PCM16 clip of two spoken sentences with a 2 s pause between them

`ptt_client.py`, a push-to-talk transcription client

```python
import asyncio
import base64
import json
import sys
import time

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

base_url, api_key, model, audio_path = sys.argv[1:5]
extra_query = {"intent": "transcription"} if len(sys.argv) > 5 and sys.argv[5] == "intent" else {}
CHUNK = 9600


def show(event: dict) -> None:
    kind = event.get("type")
    if kind in ("session.created", "session.updated", "transcription_session.created", "transcription_session.updated"):
        session = event.get("session", {})
        td = session.get("turn_detection", session.get("audio", {}).get("input", {}).get("turn_detection", "<absent>"))
        print(f"<- {kind} turn_detection={json.dumps(td)}")
    elif kind == "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed":
        print(f"<- {kind} transcript={event.get('transcript')!r}")
    elif kind == "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta":
        return
    elif kind == "error":
        print(f"<- error {json.dumps(event.get('error'))}")
    else:
        print(f"<- {kind}")


async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key)
    audio = open(audio_path, "rb").read()
    async with client.realtime.connect(model=model, extra_query=extra_query) as conn:
        update = {
            "type": "session.update",
            "session": {
                "type": "transcription",
                "audio": {
                    "input": {
                        "format": {"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 24000},
                        "turn_detection": None,
                    }
                },
            },
        }
        print(f"-> session.update turn_detection=null")
        await conn.send(update)
        for start in range(0, len(audio), CHUNK):
            await conn.send(
                {"type": "input_audio_buffer.append", "audio": base64.b64encode(audio[start : start + CHUNK]).decode()}
            )
            await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
        print(f"-> input_audio_buffer.append x{-(-len(audio) // CHUNK)} ({len(audio) / 48000:.1f}s of speech)")
        await conn.send({"type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"})
        print("-> input_audio_buffer.commit")
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 20
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            try:
                event = await asyncio.wait_for(conn.recv(), timeout=deadline - time.monotonic())
            except (asyncio.TimeoutError, Exception) as exc:
                print(f"<- (stopped: {type(exc).__name__})")
                break
            show(event.model_dump() if hasattr(event, "model_dump") else dict(event))


asyncio.run(main())
```

`voice_client.py`, a voice session that only reads back the session config

```python
import asyncio

base_url, api_key, model = sys.argv[1:4]

        update = {

        }

        await conn.send(update)

                if event.type == "session.updated":

            elif event.type == "error":
                print(f"<- error {event.error.message}")
                break


asyncio.run(main())
```

issue.title: fix(bedrock): answer 400 for service tiers Bedrock cannot serve, forward reserved
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

Bedrock models used to quietly ignore a service tier they could not use, so a request for a faster tier ran at normal speed with no warning and could still be billed at the faster price. Now that request gets a clear 400 unless the admin turned on dropping unsupported params, the reserved tier reaches Bedrock, and auto lets Bedrock pick its own default

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Bedrock Converse quietly dropped any `service_tier` it could not map
- `ultrafast` or a typo ran on Standard with a 200 and no warning
- Without `drop_params`, the dropped tier could still be billed at its higher price
- `reserved` was dropped, so reserved capacity was never used
- `auto` was rewritten to `default`

How it solves it:

- A value Bedrock cannot serve answers 400, or drops under `drop_params`
- `reserved` goes out as `serviceTier: {"type": "reserved"}`
- `standard_only` maps to `default`
- `auto` and `null` send no tier, so Bedrock serves its own default
- Bedrock batch rows honor their own `drop_params` on chat and Responses rows, and never copy it into the row Bedrock gets

Intentional product change: a request with a tier Bedrock cannot serve now fails with 400 instead of running on Standard

<details>
<summary>The decisions, with the alternatives</summary>

- `auto` sends no tier. AWS documents an omitted tier and `default` as the same Standard tier, so this keeps today's wire meaning while letting Bedrock choose. Keeping the rewrite to `default` was the alternative, and it kept a `service_tier: default` echo on the response
- An unknown value answers 400 under the `drop_params` convention every other unsupported param follows. Bedrock answers 400 for it too (a live Converse call with `ultrafast` gets `Member must satisfy enum value set: [default, priority, reserved, flex]`), so the early 400 only saves the round trip
- `fast`, OpenAI's newer name for priority, is treated like any other value Bedrock does not list. Mapping it to `priority` was the alternative, but gpt-6-luna and gpt-6.1-sol on Bedrock answer 400 for priority, so a deployment with `drop_params: true` that serves `fast` on Standard today would start failing
- Nova on the Invoke route shares this mapping, so it gets the same 400. It still never sends a valid tier to Bedrock, which is older than this PR and left for a follow-up, and `/v1/messages` on Invoke is left alone
- A Responses batch row keeps its `drop_params` by adding it back to the body the Responses bridge returns, since the bridge keeps only Responses fields. Passing it into the bridge was the alternative, but the bridge would then also drop unsupported tools, which is more than this PR changes. The passthrough branch for OpenAI-compatible models keeps `drop_params` out of the row, since Bedrock has no such field and base already sent it for chat rows
- #48860 edits the same function to refuse tiers a model is not priced for. It keeps `auto` as `default` and does not forward `reserved`, so the two fit together, and its 400 text matches this one

</details>

## User Flow

Before: a developer asks for a tier Bedrock cannot serve, gets a normal 200 on Standard, and never learns the tier was ignored

1. The admin serves `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-6-luna` with `litellm_settings.drop_params: false`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"service_tier": "ultrafast"`
3. They get 200, the response has no tier, and the request ran on Standard
4. The same request with `"service_tier": "reserved"` also returns 200 on Standard, so reserved capacity sits unused

After: the request fails fast with a 400 that names the tier, and `reserved` reaches Bedrock

1. The admin serves `bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-6-luna` with `litellm_settings.drop_params: false`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"service_tier": "ultrafast"`
3. They get 400 `does not support service_tier='ultrafast' on Bedrock`, which names `drop_params` as the way to drop it
4. `"service_tier": "reserved"` now reaches Bedrock, so an account with no reservation gets Bedrock's own 400

To keep the old quiet drop, the admin sets it on the deployment

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: bedrock/converse/us.openai.gpt-6-luna
      aws_region_name: us-east-1
      drop_params: true
```

The same `ultrafast` request to `"model": "luna"` then returns 200 on Standard, as before

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs ran at once with the same config. Each had its own Postgres, two workers sharing one Redis, and real Bedrock in us-east-1

</details>

<details>
<summary>call.py, the client (official OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs)</summary>

```python
import os
import sys

import anthropic
import openai

base, key = os.environ["PROXY_BASE_URL"], os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
route, model, tier = sys.argv[1:4]
oa = openai.OpenAI(base_url=f"{base}/v1", api_key=key, max_retries=0)
an = anthropic.Anthropic(base_url=base, api_key=key, max_retries=0)
hi = [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}]
try:
    if route == "/v1/chat/completions":
        print("200 service_tier =", oa.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=hi, max_tokens=32, service_tier=tier).service_tier)
    elif route == "/v1/responses":
        print("200 service_tier =", oa.responses.create(model=model, input="Say hi", max_output_tokens=32, service_tier=tier).service_tier)
    else:
        print("200 stop_reason =", an.messages.create(model=model, max_tokens=32, messages=hi, service_tier=tier).stop_reason)
except (openai.APIStatusError, anthropic.APIStatusError) as error:
```

```python
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import openai

base, key = os.environ["PROXY_BASE_URL"], os.environ["LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"]
url, model, tier, row_drop = sys.argv[1:5]
oa = openai.OpenAI(base_url=f"{base}/v1", api_key=key, max_retries=0)
prompt = {"input": "Say hi", "max_output_tokens": 16} if url == "/v1/responses" else {"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi"}], "max_tokens": 16}
body = {"model": model, **prompt, **({"service_tier": tier} if tier != "-" else {}), **({"drop_params": True} if row_drop == "drop" else {})}
line = json.dumps({"custom_id": "tier-row", "method": "POST", "url": url, "body": body}) + "\n"

    created = oa.files.create(file=("in.jsonl", io.BytesIO(line.encode()), "application/jsonl"), purpose="batch", extra_body={"target_model_names": model})
except openai.APIStatusError as error:

uri = re.search(r"s3://[^;,\s]+\.jsonl", decoded).group(0)
row = json.loads(subprocess.run(["aws", "s3", "cp", uri, "-", "--region", "us-west-2"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout)
model_input = row["modelInput"]
print(f"200, S3 row modelInput.serviceTier = {model_input.get('serviceTier')}, drop_params in modelInput = {'drop_params' in model_input}")
```

issue.title: fix(router): count pre-call context-window tokens with each deployment's tokenizer
issue.body:
With pre-call checks on, the router counted a prompt for any non-OpenAI deployment with gpt-3.5-turbo's tokenizer, so a prompt Cohere bills at 124,071 tokens got a local 400 as 130,613 against a 128k window

#48728 fixed this for OpenAI-only groups, and this covers every other deployment. OpenAI deployments count with their own encoding, and the rest share one GPT-4o tokenizer count that refuses locally only past 2x the window. In between, the provider decides unless a fitting deployment or an untried context window fallback can take the request

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Pre-call checks count non-OpenAI prompts with gpt-3.5-turbo's tokenizer
- Near-limit prompts the provider accepts get a local 400

How it solves it:

- Count OpenAI deployments with their own encoding
- Count the rest once with o200k_base, refusing only past 2x
- Still prefer a fitting deployment or a context window fallback

Intentional product change: a non-OpenAI deployment with nowhere else to send the request now gets a prompt our estimate puts between 1x and 2x its window, so the provider answers instead of the proxy

## User Flow

Before: a developer sending long prompts to a Cohere model through the proxy gets a 400 Cohere itself would accept

1. The proxy admin serves `cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026` (128k input window) with `enable_pre_call_checks: true`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a 551k-character prompt Cohere bills at 124,071 tokens
3. The proxy answers 400 `Context Window exceeded ... Max Input Tokens=128000, Got=130613`, and Cohere never sees it
4. /v1/responses, /v1/messages and a complexity-router `auto` model fail the same way, and a `free`-tagged request to a mixed free and paid group gets a 401

After: the same request reaches Cohere and comes back with its reply

1. The proxy admin serves `cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026` (128k input window) with `enable_pre_call_checks: true`
2. The developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a 551k-character prompt Cohere bills at 124,071 tokens
3. The proxy answers 200 with Cohere's reply
4. /v1/responses, /v1/messages, the `auto` model and the `free`-tagged request answer 200 from Cohere too, and a prompt 3x as long still gets the local 400

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs run one proxy with `--num_workers 2` and no database, on the same `.env` (`LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `COHERE_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`), differing only in the commit the proxy booted from

<details>
<summary>Setup (config, proxy, request bodies)</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-cohere
    litellm_params:
      model: cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026
      api_key: os.environ/COHERE_API_KEY
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-openai
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

router_settings:
  enable_pre_call_checks: true
```

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port $PORT --num_workers 2
git checkout b7da9a2755 && find . -name '*.md' -not -path '*/node_modules/*' | sort | xargs cat > corpus.txt
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
text = open("corpus.txt").read()[:551366] + "\n\nReply with the single word OK."
json.dump({"model": "litellm-qa-precall-cohere", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text}]}, open("cohere_body.json", "w"))
PY
jq '.stream = true' cohere_body.json > chat_cohere_stream.json
jq '{model, input: .messages[0].content, max_output_tokens: .max_tokens}' cohere_body.json > responses_cohere.json
cp cohere_body.json messages_cohere.json
jq '.messages[0].content |= ([., ., .] | join("\n"))' cohere_body.json > chat_cohere_3x.json
```

The Japanese body is built from the axe-core 4.11.4 `ja` locale (after `npm install` in ui/litellm-dashboard). Straight to the providers, Cohere bills the English body at 124,071 input tokens (HTTP 200, `MAX_TOKENS`) and OpenAI counts the Japanese body at 712,760 prompt tokens (HTTP 200, "OK"). The base already counts OpenAI models with their own encoding, so the Japanese, Replicate and 3x rows guard against regressions rather than show the fix

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
def strings(v):
    if isinstance(v, str):
        yield v
    elif isinstance(v, dict):
        for x in v.values():
            yield from strings(x)
    elif isinstance(v, list):
        for x in v:
            yield from strings(x)
ja = "\n".join(strings(json.load(open("ui/litellm-dashboard/node_modules/axe-core/locales/ja.json"))))
text = "\n".join([ja] * 53) + "\n\n最後に「OK」とだけ答えてください。"
json.dump({"model": "litellm-qa-precall-openai", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text}]}, open("openai_body.json", "w"))
PY
```

The last six cases use this second config. The Replicate key is a placeholder on purpose: the case shows the prompt reaching Replicate, which answers 401, instead of a local 400

```yaml

  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-openai

      model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna

  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-cwf
    litellm_params:
      model: cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026
      api_key: os.environ/COHERE_API_KEY
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-mixed
    litellm_params:
      model: cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026
      api_key: os.environ/COHERE_API_KEY
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-mixed
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-tagged
    litellm_params:
      model: cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026
      api_key: os.environ/COHERE_API_KEY
      tags: ["free"]
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-tagged
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.6-luna
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
      tags: ["paid"]
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-replicate
    litellm_params:
      model: replicate/meta/llama-3-70b-instruct
      api_key: r8-qa-placeholder-not-a-key

router_settings:
  enable_pre_call_checks: true
  enable_tag_filtering: true
  context_window_fallbacks: [{"litellm-qa-precall-cwf": ["litellm-qa-precall-openai"]}]
```

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
s = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog while the committee reviews the quarterly budget. "
long = s * 11000 + "\n\nReply with the single word OK."
chat = lambda m: {"model": m, "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": long}]}
json.dump(chat("litellm-qa-precall-cwf"), open("cwf_chat.json", "w"))
json.dump({"model": "litellm-qa-precall-cwf", "max_output_tokens": 16, "input": long}, open("cwf_responses.json", "w"))
json.dump(chat("litellm-qa-precall-cwf"), open("cwf_messages.json", "w"))
json.dump(chat("litellm-qa-precall-mixed"), open("mixed_chat.json", "w"))
json.dump({"model": "litellm-qa-precall-replicate", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": s * 475}]}, open("replicate_chat.json", "w"))
PY
jq '.model = "litellm-qa-precall-tagged" | .tags = ["free"]' cohere_body.json > tagged_chat.json
```

OpenAI bills the long body at 187,014 prompt tokens, between 1x and 2x Cohere's window. The Replicate body is 8,076 tokens with o200k_base, under that model's 8,192 window. The second config's cases add `-D -` to show the routing headers, filtered with `grep -v -i -E "$NOISY"`, where `NOISY='^(date|x-litellm-call-id|x-litellm-key-spend|content-security-policy|x-frame-options|x-content-type-options|llm_provider-)'`

The fallback chain cases use this third config, with `cohere_body.json`'s model set to each group

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: litellm-qa-precall-selfcwf
    litellm_params:
      model: cohere_chat/command-a-plus-05-2026
```

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 2 of 4 -->

### Medium

- Generic `fallbacks` run only after the provider answers an error
  - A prompt between 1x and 2x a non-OpenAI window reaches the provider first when only generic fallbacks are set. `context_window_fallbacks` steers it before the call
- An operator-set `max_input_tokens` on a non-OpenAI model refuses locally only past 2x
  - Treating it as exact would bring the reported 400 back, since the reporter's window is operator-set

### Low

- Complexity-router compaction still counts every prompt with cl100k
  - Its compaction trigger can disagree with what admission refuses

## Decisions

<details>
<summary>Decisions and the alternatives they beat</summary>

1. The stand-in is o200k_base, not cl100k_base
   - Across 18 languages, cl100k's worst count was 3.1x the lowest provider count (Greek), and o200k's was 1.45x (Japanese)
   - Alternative: cl100k with a margin near 3.5x, which would let a 3M-token prompt through to a 1M window
2. A stand-in count refuses locally only past 2x the window
   - 2x covers o200k's worst measured overcount and still refuses gross overflows like 3M against 1M
   - Alternative: no local refusal for stand-in models, which drops the gross-overflow protection entirely
3. A stand-in count over the window still excludes that deployment when the request has somewhere else to go
   - Somewhere else means a deployment that fits and survives the region, param and tag checks, or a context window fallback whose chain still holds a target this request has not tried, other than the failing group
   - The fallback is read the way the fallback loop reads it: the request's own `context_window_fallbacks` first, else the router's, with `disable_fallbacks` and `max_fallbacks` honored
   - Alternative: the same 2x margin on steering too, which would send mixed-window groups to the small deployment and skip configured fallbacks
4. Only OpenAI models count with their own tokenizer
   - Their tiktoken encodings ship with litellm, so counting needs no network
   - litellm's Hugging Face tokenizers (Cohere, Llama) download on first use, which stalls the worker and makes a refusal depend on whether that pod's download worked
   - Its Llama 2 tokenizer also stood in for every Replicate model, and its bundled Anthropic tokenizer is Claude 2's, which counted Russian 17% above Anthropic's count_tokens for claude-sonnet-4-5
5. Whether a deployment counts as OpenAI is read from its cost-map key, so `base_model` is honored
6. A request counts once per distinct encoding and message framing, plus one shared stand-in count
   - Framing (legacy accounting, tool section, PDF pricing) is part of the key, since a blank PDF counts 7 tokens on gpt-4o and 1541 on an OpenAI model the table does not list
   - The counts run through the router's bounded counter off the event loop, and the complexity router's admission check uses the same counter
7. OpenAI models use the encoding #48728 picks, so a new gpt-5+ name counts with o200k_base as its own tokenizer
   - The per-deployment count replaces #48728's single group-wide count in pre-call checks, and its mixed-group test now expects both deployments kept
   - Alternative: keep the group-wide count for OpenAI-only groups, which leaves two counting paths for one check
8. A `custom_tokenizer` openai encoding never overrides an OpenAI model's own encoding in `token_counter`
   - So `/utils/token_counter` and the count_tokens fallbacks keep counting gpt-4o and newer models with o200k_base
9. The fallback chain reaches pre-call checks through a context variable set around the retry call
   - The retry wrapper pops `context_window_fallbacks` from kwargs before routing, so the selection path never sees it
   - Alternative: a new kwargs flag, which every provider call path would then have to strip
10. Compaction keeps its cl100k count
    - Matching admission needs a per-deployment count on the routing context and a compactor restructure
    - Even then the 2x margin means compaction and admission would still disagree on some prompts
11. The tag-routable set is still computed on every pre-call-checked request
    - Skipping it when nothing overflows needs every window resolved twice, about 1 ms for 5 deployments, against the 13 to 88 microseconds the tag pass costs

</details>

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
