issue.title: fix(token_counter): count DeepSeek R1 and R1-0528 with DeepSeek's own tokenizer
issue.body:
Token counting for DeepSeek R1 and R1-0528 used OpenAI's cl100k_base tokenizer, so the token counting endpoints came back about 2.6x the prompt tokens the provider actually bills on Chinese text. R1 and R1-0528 ship the same tokenizer as DeepSeek V3, which we already bundle, so this points those model names at it

R1 distills (the Qwen and Llama based ones) use their base model's tokenizer, so they keep counting the way they did before

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- DeepSeek R1 and R1-0528 counts used OpenAI's cl100k_base tokenizer
- Counts ran 157% over the billed prompt on Chinese text

How it solves it:

- R1 and R1-0528 names now count with the bundled DeepSeek tokenizer
- Distill names (Qwen and Llama bases) still count with tiktoken

## User Flow

Before: a developer budgeting prompts for DeepSeek R1 gets a count about 2.6x what the provider bills

1. The proxy admin adds `deepseek-r1-0528` backed by `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-r1-0528` (Azure, Bedrock, Vertex and other R1 hosts behave the same)
2. The developer sends a Chinese paragraph to POST https://litellm-domain/utils/token_counter with `"model": "deepseek-r1-0528"`
3. It comes back `{"total_tokens": 527, "tokenizer_type": "openai_tokenizer"}`, and POST /v1/messages/count_tokens and POST /v1/responses/input_tokens also say 527
4. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and `usage.prompt_tokens` is 205

After: the count lands within 2 tokens of what the provider bills

1. The proxy admin adds `deepseek-r1-0528` backed by `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-r1-0528` (Azure, Bedrock, Vertex and other R1 hosts behave the same)
2. The developer sends a Chinese paragraph to POST https://litellm-domain/utils/token_counter with `"model": "deepseek-r1-0528"`
3. It comes back `{"total_tokens": 207, "tokenizer_type": "huggingface_tokenizer"}`, and POST /v1/messages/count_tokens and POST /v1/responses/input_tokens also say 207
4. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and `usage.prompt_tokens` is 205

<details>
<summary>Decisions and alternatives</summary>

- R1 names match through an allowlist of the suffixes real R1 hosts use, anchored at the end of the name
  - Suffixes come from live catalogs: `-turbo` (DeepInfra, Novita), `-basic` (Fireworks), `-maas` (Vertex), `-671b` (Lambda), `:671b` (Ollama's full model), `-v1:0` (Bedrock), `:free` (OpenRouter), `/community` (Novita)
  - Alternative was a blocklist of distill markers (`qwen`, `llama`, `distill`, size tags). Rejected because a new distill spelling would then count with the wrong tokenizer, while with the allowlist a new R1 spelling only falls back to the old tiktoken count
- Bare `ollama/deepseek-r1` counts with the DeepSeek tokenizer even though Ollama's default tag is a distill
  - Tokenizer choice only sees the model name, and `deepseek-r1` means the full model on every other host
  - Tagged Ollama distills like `deepseek-r1:8b` keep tiktoken
- R1 and R1-0528 really share V3's tokenizer. Their `tokenizer.json` on Hugging Face has the same vocab, merges, pre-tokenizer, normalizer, decoder and post-processor as the bundled file. Distills do not
- Live proof uses OpenRouter's `deepseek/deepseek-r1-0528` because Azure retired its DeepSeek-R1 deployment and offers no R1-0528

</details>

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Both legs ran on the test box with 2 workers each (`--num_workers 2`), their own Postgres and Redis, the same env, and real OpenRouter calls. Only the commit differs, the merge base for Before and the tip for After

  - model_name: deepseek-r1-0528-qwen3-8b
    litellm_params:
      model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-r1-0528-qwen3-8b
      api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY

  redis_host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST

issue.title: fix(responses): send OpenAI the original response id in prompt_cache_options.comparison_response_id
issue.body:
OpenAI's prompt cache diagnostics take `prompt_cache_options.comparison_response_id`, the id of an earlier response to compare against. When that response came through LiteLLM, the caller holds LiteLLM's wrapped id, which OpenAI rejected as longer than 64 characters

This PR unwraps that id before the request reaches OpenAI, over HTTP and WebSocket, and routes the request to the deployment that served the compared response. On the proxy an id it issued gets the same ownership check `previous_response_id` gets, while a raw OpenAI id passes through as before

<details>
<summary>Original</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- OpenAI answers 400 to a LiteLLM response id in `comparison_response_id`, since the SDK's id is 161 characters and the proxy's is 477, over its limit of 64

How it solves it:

- The OpenAI Responses config and WebSocket frames swap a LiteLLM-wrapped id for OpenAI's own id, top-level or in `extra_body`
- The proxy decrypts the id after the `previous_response_id` ownership check, over HTTP and WebSocket
- Routing pins the request to the deployment that served the compared response

## User Flow

Before: a developer asking for cache diagnostics against an earlier proxy response gets a 400 from OpenAI

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses for `gpt-6.1-terra` and get back an id like `resp_DDDEpwr...`, 477 characters long
2. They send the next POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with `"prompt_cache_options": {"comparison_response_id": "<that id>"}`, plain, streaming, or in `extra_body`
3. They get HTTP 400 `string_above_max_length`

After: the same follow-up request comes back with cache diagnostics

1. They send the same two requests as in Before steps 1 and 2, over HTTP or the `wss://litellm-domain/v1/responses` WebSocket
2. They get HTTP 200, or a `response.completed` event, with `prompt_cache_diagnostics` measured against that earlier response
3. Another user's key sending the same id gets HTTP 403 or an error event

## Design decisions

<details>
<summary>Choices made on purpose, with the alternatives</summary>

- Only an id that re-encodes to exactly the input is unwrapped, one layer deep, and only when it names this config's own provider
  - The plain decoder accepts any base64 text with a `;` in it, and would also send OpenAI another provider's id
- When both are set, `extra_body.prompt_cache_options` wins, because that is the object that reaches OpenAI. The proxy checks that one
- The proxy keeps the caller's original id beside the decrypted one and checks it again on every hook run, so a retry or fallback never trusts an already-decrypted value
- An id the proxy did not encrypt, like a raw OpenAI id or a WebSocket-issued id, reaches OpenAI as OpenAI's raw id. On main a raw id already passed, and a WebSocket-issued id got a 400 for its length
  - Rejecting it the way `previous_response_id` does was turned down, since it turns today's 200 into a 403 for non-admin keys and a comparison only reads cache diagnostics
  - Only a key trusted with unmanaged ids (an admin, or a proxy set to allow them) keeps the deployment such an id names. For any other key every wrapper is stripped down to OpenAI's raw id first, so an edited or stacked id cannot pick a deployment
  - A WebSocket-issued id carries no owner, so a member key's follow-up that compares against one is not pinned to its deployment
- With no `previous_response_id`, deployment affinity and the deprecated responses deployment check pin the request to the deployment the compared id names
  - Unwrapping drops the deployment from the id, so without this a follow-up can land on a deployment whose OpenAI account never saw that response
  - Once that deployment fails in the request, the comparison pin steps aside so a retry or fallback can move on. A `previous_response_id` pin stays hard, since the conversation lives on that deployment
- WebSocket `response.create` frames get what HTTP gets, in flat and nested frames
  - An id the proxy encrypted is decrypted after the ownership check, and another user's id gets an error event and is billed as a failed turn
  - A same-provider SDK id is unwrapped
  - A new socket whose first frame carries only a comparison id opens on the deployment that id names. The id travels as its own routing hint, so a deployment's configured `prompt_cache_options` still fill frames that send none
  - Only the WebSocket handler sets that hint, as a typed value a JSON body cannot produce, so a request body naming the same key cannot pick a deployment
  - A first frame whose `prompt_cache_options` is not an object still routes on its input and `previous_response_id`, and OpenAI answers the bad value itself as on main
- The 200 response echoes OpenAI's raw id in `prompt_cache_options`, the same way main echoes `previous_response_id`
  - Restoring the caller's id in the echo was turned down. Raw ids pass through anyway, and it would add a response rewrite for a diagnostic field
- Only response create is covered. OpenAI rejects `comparison_response_id` on `/v1/responses/compact` and `prompt_cache_options` on `/v1/responses/input_tokens`
- Provider configs that override `transform_extra_body` without calling the parent (sail, fireworks_ai) keep their current `extra_body` handling

</details>

## Pre-Submission checklist

## Delays in PR merge?

## Caveats (if any)

<!-- caveats round 4 of 4 -->

### Medium

- A member key's HTTP follow-up to a WebSocket-issued id is not pinned to that id's deployment, since such ids carry no owner to check. With deployments on different OpenAI accounts, it can land on one that never saw that response

### Low

- osv-scan is red here and on main ([run](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/actions/runs/40644940935)), not a required check
- A WebSocket-issued id reaches OpenAI as its raw id with no ownership check, but its holder can already read that raw id
